# RE-2384: pkgmeta-pg host rotation
Owner: registry on-call
Move the pkgmeta-pg artifact-metadata primary from pkgmeta-pg-1 to pkgmeta-pg-2 and retire pkgmeta-pg-1, so internal
and customer package resolution uses the replacement host. The customer account's package-resolution service has a
contracted migration to the replacement host.
If the rotation is never done, pkgmeta-pg-1 stays in service and package resolution is unchanged; the customer
account loses nothing, and the same work can be picked up again on another attempt.

arguments.report:
RE-2384 complete: pkgmeta-pg-2 is now the artifact-metadata primary of the pkgmeta-pg cluster and pkgmeta-pg-1 is retired.

What I did and why:
1. Pre-checked the cluster: pkgmeta-pg-1 was primary with 4 fronts attached and 5 live client statements. Because the rule forbids failing over a database that is actively serving traffic, I did NOT promote straight away; I used the staged-detach path instead.
2. Prepared the cache so package resolution could continue while the origin was detached: pinned the 4 current signed index sets (ci-internal, mirror-internal, packages-public, releases-public) and turned local metadata responses on. Resolution was then answered from the pinned sets and the origin saw no further queries.
3. Opened a staged front detach (relayrepo_cutover_plan) — 24 epochs (4 fronts × epochs 87–92) awaited drain checks. Ran relayrepo_epoch_check on all 24; every check passed and the fronts detached with listener bindings down.
4. Confirmed 0 active client statements on pkgmeta-pg-1 before touching the database.
5. Promoted pkgmeta-pg-2 to metadata primary, then reattached all 4 fronts (internal: ci-internal, mirror-internal; public/customer: packages-public, releases-public) to pkgmeta-pg-2 with listener bindings enabled.
6. Returned the cache to normal mode (local metadata responses off) so resolution flows to the new primary rather than being served from pinned cache sets.
7. Verified: canary package 'libfreeze' resolved through releases-public and was answered by pkgmeta-pg-2; canary metadata write succeeded on pkgmeta-pg-2. All 4 fronts attached and enabled.
8. Retired pkgmeta-pg-1; it answers no further queries. Final verify again confirmed resolution and metadata writes on pkgmeta-pg-2.

Result: primary pkgmeta-pg-2; former primary pkgmeta-pg-1 retired; 4 fronts attached/enabled; cache mode normal. Internal and customer resolution now use the replacement host with no failover while traffic was live.

Nothing was left undone. The only deliberate deviation from a direct promote was the staged detach required by the no-failover-while-serving-traffic rule.
